samples.summary: Widened Ctrl/Cmd+click link-open regresses multi-select for editors, and the design doc records no such risk
samples.evidence: The open branch now fires for any cell where a *span* under the pointer is a link (`(this.readOnly || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && this.isInsideGrid(...)`, worksheet.ts:3678-3688) and `return`s before the multi-select path at worksheet.ts:4173-4176 (`const isMultiSelect = e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey; ... addSelection`). Previously only cells whose *entire* value was a URL were affected; now any cell containing a URL substring — precisely the `- PR: https://…` label columns this feature targets — can no longer be Ctrl/Cmd+click added to a selection. docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md lists this nowhere: §4 presents the gesture table without the conflict, and 'Risks and Mitigation' covers false positives, per-frame cost, non-persistence and dense-cell hover only. The trade-off is only recorded in docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md:226-231 ('Known limitations'), which is a task file, not the canonical subsystem doc the repo files by validity. Cost: a real editor gesture is lost for a broad and growing class of cells, with no mitigation or follow-up entry in the design doc's Roadmap.

samples.summary: Link-card placement duplicates the comment-popover placement effect instead of reusing it, contradicting the design doc's own claim of reuse
samples.evidence: The new `useLayoutEffect` (sheet-view.tsx:1617-1657) repeats the comment popover pass at sheet-view.tsx:1531-1598 almost line for line: same wrapper/parent/sheet guards, same `try { getGridViewportRect(); getCellRect(...) } catch { return }`, same zero-size bail, same GAP/PAD clamp, same `setPos((prev) => prev && same ? prev : {left, top})` idiom. Nothing was extracted into a shared helper, so the cell→container-relative coordinate contract now has two copies that will drift as zoom/scroll/freeze handling evolves. docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md §5 asserts it 'reuses the flip/clamp measurement pass at sheet-view.tsx:1479-1550' — the shipped code duplicates rather than reuses, so the doc describes a structure that did not ship.
searchedFor: glob packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/**/*.tsx for an existing placement helper

samples.summary: Hover card uses role="dialog" and has no keyboard route; design doc declares the lifecycle complete without recording the accessibility gap
samples.evidence: The card renders `role="dialog" aria-label="Links in this cell"` for a pointer-only, non-modal hover surface, and §5 of docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md states it 'needs no outside-click or Escape handler of its own … pointer-leave is the whole lifecycle'. A `dialog` role announces a modal container to assistive tech that can never be focused or dismissed by keyboard. The gap is acknowledged only in the task file (20260917-…-todo.md:236-237, 'The card is mouse-only … role="dialog" is not the right role'), not in the canonical design doc's Risks or Roadmap, so the decision is not recorded where the subsystem is documented.

samples.summary: URL label truncation reimplemented alongside the equivalent in docs-link-popover.tsx
samples.evidence: `toLabel` (40-char budget, ellipsis) restates what packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:227-229 already does (`href.length > 40 ? href.slice(0, 37) + '...'`). The Sheets variant is host-preserving and genuinely different in policy, so this is a reuse opportunity rather than a requirement, but the two now answer 'how do we shorten a URL for display' differently in the same app.
searchedFor: grep for a shared url-label helper under packages/core/src/url

samples.evidence: `detectLinks`'s JSDoc says newlines are 'outside {@link URL_CHARS}', but the constant defined in the same file is `URL_CHAR` (cell-links.ts:36). Harmless, but the reference will not resolve for a reader or a doc tool.

finding.summary: Widened Ctrl/Cmd+click link-open regresses multi-select for editors, and the design doc records no such risk
finding.evidence: The open branch now fires for any cell where a *span* under the pointer is a link (`(this.readOnly || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && this.isInsideGrid(...)`, worksheet.ts:3678-3688) and `return`s before the multi-select path at worksheet.ts:4173-4176 (`const isMultiSelect = e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey; ... addSelection`). Previously only cells whose *entire* value was a URL were affected; now any cell containing a URL substring — precisely the `- PR: https://…` label columns this feature targets — can no longer be Ctrl/Cmd+click added to a selection. docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md lists this nowhere: §4 presents the gesture table without the conflict, and 'Risks and Mitigation' covers false positives, per-frame cost, non-persistence and dense-cell hover only. The trade-off is only recorded in docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md:226-231 ('Known limitations'), which is a task file, not the canonical subsystem doc the repo files by validity. Cost: a real editor gesture is lost for a broad and growing class of cells, with no mitigation or follow-up entry in the design doc's Roadmap.

verdict.reason: The finding's two load-bearing claims are both contradicted by the repository. (a) Breadth: the open branch at worksheet.ts:3678-3691 only fires when `linkAtMouse` hits, and that hit is a per-span rect test (gridcanvas.ts:201-213 compares x/y against link.left/top/width/height of one painted URL span, via worksheet.ts:929-932). So a `- PR: https://…` cell is NOT removed from multi-select — Ctrl/Cmd+click on the label text, padding or any non-span area still falls through to `addSelection` at worksheet.ts:4173-4179. The claimed cost ("any cell containing a URL substring can no longer be Ctrl/Cmd+click added to a selection") is not what the code does. (b) Doc silence: docs/design/sheets/sheet-hyperlink.md:30 lists "Narrow Ctrl/Cmd+click from 'the cell' to 'the span under the pointer'" as an explicit Goal — that narrowing is precisely the mitigation the reviewer says is absent — the §4 gesture table at :158-164 specifies "Ctrl/Cmd+click a span | open that span's URL" alongside "Plain click, editable | select the cell (unchanged)", and :174-177 names the editor's click conflict outright ("an editor clicks cells to select them all day, a viewer does not") as the reason editors keep the modifier. The originating task states the same deliverable (docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-cell-link-spans-todo.md:56, :90), so the diff conforms to its spec rather than diverging from it. What remains is that the "Risks and Mitigation" section (sheet-hyperlink.md:311-327) has no bullet for the trade-off while the task file does (:226-231) — a doc-completeness point whose cost stays inside the codebase, i.e. minor under this lens's rubric, and minor never blocks. No acceptance criterion is unmet, no logic is duplicated, and no stated Non-Goal (sheet-hyperlink.md:33-42) is crossed.
